# hubspot_property (Resource)

Manages a custom CRM property definition (`/crm/v3/properties/{objectType}`). Requires the `crm.schemas.{objectType}.write` scope for the target object type (e.g. `crm.schemas.contacts.write`).

**Destroy archives, it does not delete**: HubSpot soft-deletes properties, and an archived property's name stays reserved for roughly 90 days ("name purgatory"). Re-creating a property with a recently archived name fails until the archived property is purged or restored in the HubSpot UI.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# An enumeration property on contacts. Option list position is the display
# order: reorder the list to reorder the options in the HubSpot UI.
resource "hubspot_property" "example" {
  object_type = "contacts"
  name        = "customer_tier"
  label       = "Customer Tier"
  type        = "enumeration"
  field_type  = "select"
  group_name  = "contactinformation"
  description = "Commercial tier of the contact."

  options = [
    { label = "Bronze", value = "bronze" },
    { label = "Silver", value = "silver" },
    {
      label       = "Gold"
      value       = "gold"
      description = "Top tier."
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `field_type` (String) UI control used to edit the property: `text`, `textarea`, `number`, `date`, `select`, `radio`, `checkbox`, `booleancheckbox`, `file`, `html`, `phonenumber`, or `calculation_equation`. Mutable within the same `type`.
- `group_name` (String) Name of the property group the property is displayed under.
- `label` (String) Human-readable label shown in the HubSpot UI.
- `name` (String) Internal property name. Changing this forces replacement, which archives the old property and **destroys the data stored in it on every record**. The archived name also stays reserved for ~90 days, blocking immediate reuse.
- `object_type` (String) CRM object type the property belongs to (e.g. `contacts`, `companies`, `deals`, `tickets`, or a custom object type ID). Changing this forces replacement.
- `type` (String) Data type of the property: `string`, `number`, `bool`, `enumeration`, `date`, or `datetime`. Changing this forces replacement (destroys record data).

### Optional

- `description` (String) Description shown to users in the HubSpot UI.
- `display_order` (Number) Position of the property within its group (lower sorts first). When unset, HubSpot assigns `-1` (unordered). Note HubSpot rewrites `0` to `-1` server-side.
- `form_field` (Boolean) Whether the property can be used in HubSpot forms. Defaults to `false`.
- `has_unique_value` (Boolean) Whether values must be unique across records. Defaults to `false`. Changing this forces replacement (destroys record data).
- `hidden` (Boolean) Whether the property is hidden in the HubSpot UI. Defaults to `false`.
- `options` (Attributes List) Ordered choices for `enumeration` properties. **List position is the display order** — reorder the list to reorder options. Option identity is `value`; changing a value orphans record data stored under the old value. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--options))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Composite identifier in the form `{object_type}/{name}`.

<a id="nestedatt--options"></a>
### Nested Schema for `options`

Required:

- `label` (String) Label shown for this choice in the HubSpot UI.
- `value` (String) Internal value stored on records. Identifies the option.

Optional:

- `description` (String) Description of this choice.
- `hidden` (Boolean) Whether the choice is hidden in the HubSpot UI. Defaults to `false`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Properties are imported using "{object_type}/{name}".
terraform import hubspot_property.example 'contacts/customer_tier'
```
